newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Slovak PM warns Euro groups off minorities issues.
newsitem.headline: Slovak PM warns Euro groups off minorities issues.

text.p: Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said on Friday the Council of Europe should set standards for treatment of minorities, warning that other European bodies only complicated matters by getting involved.

"The Council of Europe adopted the framework convention on the rights of national minorities and...we are in favour of all European countries ratifying this convention," Meciar, whose country has been criticised for its treatment of minorities, particularly its 600,000-strong Hungarian community, said at a summit of the Central European Initiative (CEI) in Austria.
Meciar, responding during a news conference to a question on why Slovakia and the Czech Republic had failed to sign a CEI resolution on minorities, said he did not think the CEI should be involved.
He said resolutions adopted by other pan-European groups other than the Council of Europe risked setting "partial or regional standards that could overlap".
"The CEI should not deal with the question of minorities," he said.
The CEI is a grouping of 16 eastern and central European nations established in 1989 to find common approaches to political, economic and social problems.
